# ============================================================
# MICROGLIAL COMPOSITION ANALYSIS — snRNA-seq
# DAM vs Homeostatic microglia | Pearson chi-square tests
# ============================================================

# STEP 01 — PACKAGES AND OUTPUT DIRECTORY --------------------
# install.packages(c("ggplot2", "dplyr", "tidyr"))
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

output_dir <- "Microglia_ChiSquare_Results"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# STEP 02 — INPUT DATA ---------------------------------------
# Percentages are rounded values from plots. If exact per-cell
# assignments are available, use actual counts instead.
microglia_table <- data.frame(
  Group = c("WT", "Control", "PAP1", "PBS", "ShK"),
  Total_cells = c(200, 1005, 836, 1366, 705),
  DAM_percent = c(11.0, 57.3, 60.4, 57.4, 70.2),
  Homeostatic_percent = c(89.0, 42.7, 39.6, 42.6, 29.8)
)
stopifnot(all(abs(microglia_table$DAM_percent +
                  microglia_table$Homeostatic_percent - 100) < 1e-8))

# STEP 03 — RECONSTRUCT CELL COUNTS ---------------------------
microglia_table <- microglia_table %>%
  mutate(
    DAM = round(Total_cells * DAM_percent / 100),
    Homeostatic = Total_cells - DAM,
    DAM_percent_reconstructed = 100 * DAM / Total_cells,
    Homeostatic_percent_reconstructed = 100 * Homeostatic / Total_cells
  )
print(microglia_table)
write.csv(microglia_table,
          file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_Composition_Table.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# STEP 04 — BUILD CONTINGENCY TABLES --------------------------
make_contingency <- function(group1, group2, dat = microglia_table) {
  chosen <- dat[match(c(group1, group2), dat$Group), ]
  if (anyNA(chosen$Group)) stop("One or more group names not found")
  tab <- as.matrix(chosen[, c("DAM", "Homeostatic")])
  rownames(tab) <- chosen$Group
  colnames(tab) <- c("DAM", "Homeostatic")
  tab
}

WT_Control <- make_contingency("WT", "Control")
PAP1_Control <- make_contingency("PAP1", "Control")
ShK_PBS <- make_contingency("ShK", "PBS")

print(WT_Control)
print(PAP1_Control)
print(ShK_PBS)

write.csv(WT_Control, file.path(output_dir, "Contingency_WT_vs_Control.csv"))
write.csv(PAP1_Control, file.path(output_dir, "Contingency_PAP1_vs_Control.csv"))
write.csv(ShK_PBS, file.path(output_dir, "Contingency_ShK_vs_PBS.csv"))

# STEP 05 — PEARSON CHI-SQUARE TESTS --------------------------
# correct = FALSE reproduces the original analysis.
# Chi-square assumes independent observations; pooled nuclei from
# the same mouse are not independent biological replicates.
test_WT_Control <- chisq.test(WT_Control, correct = FALSE)
test_PAP1_Control <- chisq.test(PAP1_Control, correct = FALSE)
test_ShK_PBS <- chisq.test(ShK_PBS, correct = FALSE)

print(test_WT_Control)
print(test_PAP1_Control)
print(test_ShK_PBS)

# STEP 06 — COMBINE TEST RESULTS ------------------------------
tests <- list(
  "WT vs Control" = test_WT_Control,
  "PAP1 vs Control" = test_PAP1_Control,
  "ShK vs PBS" = test_ShK_PBS
)

results <- data.frame(
  Comparison = names(tests),
  Chi_square = vapply(tests, function(x) unname(x$statistic), numeric(1)),
  df = vapply(tests, function(x) unname(x$parameter), numeric(1)),
  P_value = vapply(tests, function(x) x$p.value, numeric(1)),
  Min_expected_count = vapply(tests, function(x) min(x$expected), numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)

# STEP 07 — MULTIPLE TESTING CORRECTION -----------------------
results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    FDR = p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"),
    Significance = case_when(
      FDR < 0.0001 ~ "****",
      FDR < 0.001 ~ "***",
      FDR < 0.01 ~ "**",
      FDR < 0.05 ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  )
print(results)
write.csv(results,
          file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_ChiSquare_Results_BH_FDR.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# STEP 08 — LONG-FORM COMPOSITION TABLE ----------------------
plot_df <- microglia_table %>%
  select(Group, Total_cells, DAM, Homeostatic) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(DAM, Homeostatic),
               names_to = "State", values_to = "Cells") %>%
  mutate(
    Group = factor(Group, levels = c("WT", "Control", "PAP1", "PBS", "ShK")),
    State = factor(State, levels = c("Homeostatic", "DAM")),
    Percent = 100 * Cells / Total_cells
  )
write.csv(plot_df,
          file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_Composition_Long.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# STEP 09 — STACKED PERCENTAGE BAR PLOT -----------------------
p_composition <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = Percent, fill = State)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percent, 1), "%")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Homeostatic = "#4477AA", DAM = "#CC6677")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Microglial composition (%)", fill = "Cell state") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
print(p_composition)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_Stacked_Composition.pdf"),
       p_composition, width = 7.5, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_Stacked_Composition.png"),
       p_composition, width = 7.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)

# STEP 10 — DAM PERCENTAGE BAR PLOT ---------------------------
dam_df <- microglia_table %>%
  mutate(Group = factor(Group, levels = c("WT", "Control", "PAP1", "PBS", "ShK")))

p_dam <- ggplot(dam_df, aes(x = Group, y = DAM_percent_reconstructed)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#CC6677", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", DAM_percent_reconstructed)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 85), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "DAM microglia (%)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13)
print(p_dam)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "DAM_Percentage_Barplot.pdf"),
       p_dam, width = 7, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "DAM_Percentage_Barplot.png"),
       p_dam, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

# STEP 11 — COMPARISON-SPECIFIC PLOTS -------------------------
comparison_groups <- list(
  "WT_vs_Control" = c("WT", "Control"),
  "PAP1_vs_Control" = c("PAP1", "Control"),
  "ShK_vs_PBS" = c("ShK", "PBS")
)

for (nm in names(comparison_groups)) {
  groups <- comparison_groups[[nm]]
  tmp <- plot_df %>%
    filter(as.character(Group) %in% groups) %>%
    mutate(Group = factor(as.character(Group), levels = groups))
  p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(x = Group, y = Percent, fill = State)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.65, color = "white") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Homeostatic = "#4477AA", DAM = "#CC6677")) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = gsub("_", " ", nm), x = NULL,
         y = "Microglial composition (%)", fill = "Cell state") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13)
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0(nm, "_Composition.pdf")),
         p, width = 5, height = 5)
}

# STEP 12 — SAVE REPRODUCIBILITY INFORMATION ------------------
saveRDS(list(composition = microglia_table,
             contingency = list(WT_Control = WT_Control,
                                PAP1_Control = PAP1_Control,
                                ShK_PBS = ShK_PBS),
             tests = tests,
             results = results),
        file.path(output_dir, "Microglia_ChiSquare_Analysis.rds"))
capture.output(sessionInfo(),
               file = file.path(output_dir, "R_Session_Info.txt"))
message("Analysis completed. Results saved in: ", normalizePath(output_dir))

# NOTE: For biological inference, analyze counts per mouse rather than
# pooled cells, e.g. using a binomial mixed model with mouse as a
# biological unit, or an appropriate replicate-level approach.
